Three Pitborn aces fly the existing raider, reaver, and bruiser hulls and come back with their yard lines.
Commander Lusk returns on a lawful cutter that leaves a clean pilot alone, and Adjudicator Ost flies with a Helix invoice line.
Dock hands name Clatter, Big Ballast, Ratchet Lu, Lusk, and Ost in their home bars while each route window is open.
Rock rain, slag spill, and lantern drift take over their arenas with the same install shape as the rooms they were copied from.
Reef surge, the shepherd pulse, and Sprocket's crate play in the lattice, the hive, and Helios Core.
Three quiet hulls in Charon, Sker, and Tethys pay spore catalyst, scrap, and consumer goods when the hold is taken.
The Codex, Page Nine, and Due Diligence pay their named salvage and do not steal another wreck's unique.
Helix contacts use the Concord grammar and say lawful interdiction, under orders, read the invoice.
A Helix ship answers a hail in the Directorate's invoice voice on every stance.
Pulling a declared trick unlocks that feat once. Saying the same episode again announces nothing.
A witnessed cargo-pod kill names its pilot Shellwright.
The first ship you release under load into another hull unlocks Two Hulls, One Rope.
The first kill by the mass still on the line unlocks Keep the Heavy End Moving.
The first hull killed crossing a loaded tether unlocks Watch the Cable.
One throw that wrecks three or more hulls unlocks One Mistake, Three Wrecks.
The first kill-shot you clear by a hair unlocks Still Flying.
The first hostile you tow into a fatal collision unlocks Dragged All the Way In.
The first body you redirect into terrain for the kill unlocks The Rock Won.
The first body a gravity well carries into a kill unlocks Out the Other Side.
The first wreck you put back in motion for a kill unlocks One Job Left.
The first banked shot around cover that kills unlocks Cover Is Not a Guarantee.
The first hostile ordnance you return to kill its owner unlocks Back With Your Name On It.
The first escape that rides a blast clear of a threat unlocks Rode the Blast.
The first escape through a moving gap between two hulls unlocks You Fit.
The first body you correct with a second impulse into a kill unlocks Second Impulse.
The first rope-to-well-to-wreck kill unlocks Rope, Well, Wreck.
The first Twin Bridle pair you drive into terrain unlocks Two Hulls, One Rope, One Rock.
The first shoved wreck that kills a hull of its own faction unlocks His Own Wingman.
The first razor-rated release that kills unlocks Perfect Cut.
When a capital fight starts, one receipt names the boss and its lesson.
When a capital fight changes acts, one receipt names the new act.
Breaking a part that cancels a cast names the attack you stopped.
An unmoored throw window calls itself exposed and names the beat.
A fully disarmed boss says so once. Coming back from a pause does not repeat it.
When a capital wing arrives, its authored bark is spoken once.
A boss strike that lands on you names itself. A strike on someone else stays quiet.
A hostile line on your hull reads LINE ON YOU. Your own latch still reads as your massline.
A swarm capital fight fields its throw-mass wreckage once. A second start does not double it.
The Scar Bazaar posts the surplus-move job on the Kepler flight deck.
The Shadow Cache posts the shrine-readings job in Orcus Shadow.
The Haumea observatory posts the fracture-reading job at the ice fissure.
Nereid posts the same-shift ice job between the shoal and the waystation.
The Quiet den posts the well-sounding job in Proteus Well.
Eunomia posts the licensed-plate job, and the fence keeps its black market.
A lane stranger called Grandma hails just to talk, with no cargo and no ask.
A crew found on a dead relay hails and talks, and asks for nothing.
A returning ace names the weapon that downed them. An ace without that memory stays quiet.
A hunter you have escaped twice names the streak. A fresh hunter does not.
A repeat career close names the lap. The first circuit still reads the old line.
Unmasked Helix ships answer in their own invoice voice: lawful interdiction, under orders, read the invoice first.
Flying into Charon, Sker, Tethys, Pallas, or Dione charts the activity hull there and speaks its scan line.
Spore catalyst and gate handshakes show as living samples and lattice credentials instead of ordinary freight.
Asking at Research Station Veil names Page Nine, and Ashfall names the Charon garden while Big Ballast is off the lane.
A hold of spore catalyst or a live specimen reads as Concord risk, Frontier wary, and Quiet favor instead of a blank conscience.
A hard hit cracks spore catalyst and the unbroken lens into scoopable spill, and leaves iron ore and a gate handshake in the hold.
Dumping spore catalyst, a live specimen, or filament leaves a green pod that eats hull on contact, and ore stays inert.
Fauna in the Veil null corridor scatter where the pocket actually sits, including far from the sector origin.
The Veil containment core stays alive; only the seal ring around it scatters fauna.
A broken directive and a revoked route name themselves on the scanner instead of looking like strangers.
An exception grant renames the machine as route authority on file, not as a witnessed contact.
The Veil revoked gate says the route is closed, and flying out does not count as obeying.
A witness mark stays on file, but a fault makes the Veil gate auditor ask again.
The first Charon pylon sighting announces the observed scan label, not a compliance grade you have not earned.
When a claim fight falls apart, the yard says the raid is still coming and how long you have to get back.
A loss headline names the house that lost the hull, including Helix and the Archive, and an unknown house is no longer called A a ship.
Shooting a bounty hunter while the jump spool is winding tells you the spool was interrupted.
In an Io Reach fight, the director still calls it a fight after a long quiet log.
A fight queued at Sker does not count as combat waiting for you at Helios.
Helios's sector report names the Memorial Array anomaly instead of saying the hazards are clear.
The open Veil to Ashfall wormhole plots as one gate hop, not a long drift.
When Ceres and Io cost the same fuel, the route goes through the quieter Tethys junction.
When two tar clouds overlap, the escape cue points at the one you are deepest in.
Your reserved pad at Helios stays yours when the next ship arrives.
A hauler still in the Helios yard after midnight stays on the board.
Scanning the veil rays at Quiet Ice makes them flinch and keep fleeing.
Gunfire breaks the needle swarm's ring and they run, while a veil ray nearby stays put.
An archive crab builds a debris pile you can read, and the pile falls when the crab dies.
A wake eel's trail pulls a cold furnace maw in, and the maw charges.
Towing a suture mite off its seam and letting go leaves it defensive.
When a stone lung exhales, nearby grazers break off and feed on the plume.
Glassbacks read as scattered glass until you get close, and the stone lung beside them keeps its name.
Close to a cold bell, it names itself and tolls before the radiation front.
Recovering the Cinder Nursery recorder does not wipe a fault already on your standing.
Veil step stops in front of a solid wreck instead of dropping the hull inside it.
Docking at the den with hot cargo and not enough credits now says the cut and leaves the pod hot.
The salvage cradle says Stellarite Ore when that core lands in the bay, instead of the raw ore id.
Clearing a loaded lane names the ore you would lose and waits for a second confirm.
Pouring a fuel cell into a tank that cannot take it now says how much room is left, and a booked pump says it already owns the gap.
A core in a hollow hall cuts its output from heat, the claim says so on the first watch, and the board no longer calls that machine idle.
A drone whose hold is full hails Reach Station by name instead of calling a named berth a depot.
A cradle set into a full salvage bay keeps the core and the units that did not fit, and finishes them once the bay has room.

Entering Charon Expanse, Sker Haven or Tethys Junction has the dock speak the garden hull, ballast barge or Re-router rumor and chart its bearing — and the unique-wreck census now stays green over all 22 authored hulls.

The six open factions — Understory, Fulfillment, Archive, Pitborn, Free Frontier, Verge-Layers — now have canon sketches in the canonical factions file, each marked PROVISIONAL (R10, 2026-10-21), so the story bible the narrative lane writes from finally matches the fourteen factions the game fields.
Breaking an enemy part names that part. Your own ship still uses the long sentences.
Hours 11-15 of the research ladder are authored verbs from existing late nodes. Seeds 4242 and 15510 see the same rows.
A latch whose open segment crosses a live wreck or station hull is refused, and a sidestep that clears the hull opens the line.
A ship wrecked by the player's thrown mass says so. An NPC-on-NPC crash keeps the old line.
Thrown mass on a swarm champion tears a rotating capital part. Mission fights stay on the same rotation.
Recipes that fire in the first hour caption as authored sentences. None fall through to an id-built line.
Incoming telegraph, repulsor deployed, and massline captions are in the source inventory a translation pass can read.
A telegraph from 8 o'clock captions as 8 o'clock, using the same position that pans the cue.
A committed jump, an arrival, and an interdiction each emit one caption. Repeats inside the dedupe window stay one.
A crushing massline hit reads heavier than a solid hit, and a glance is the lightest, on the existing impact lane.
A kill by another ship does not file as your Kill clip. A kill you make still does.
Your death files one Death clip. A hit that does not kill you files none.
